What to bring — curated for a premium sensory experience

We provide luxe bolsters and blankets, but for your comfort bring: a yoga mat or travel rug, an eye pillow (or we provide a cooling eye mask), cozy socks, and an optional light blanket. For VIP Day bookings consider a personal scarf or essential oil for scent anchoring.

The flow — what a session feels like

Arrival & settling (15 min) → Intention setting (5–10 min) → Immersive sound journey with hand-crafted instruments (40–55 min) → Gentle re-orientation and tea (10–15 min). Our facilitators dim lights, layer tones, and guide breath to create a deep bodily resonance.

We will respond within 48 hours. For urgent booking calls, please ring us at {{PHONE}}.
Contraindications & safety
Sound baths are gentle but powerful. If you are pregnant, have a pacemaker, severe tinnitus, epilepsy, or are currently under heavy psychiatric medication, consult your physician before attending and notify our facilitator upon booking. By booking you confirm awareness of these guidelines.

Signature Instruments

Our public gatherings rotate an intentional palette: hand-tuned crystal bowls, koshi chimes, a chromatic monochord, ocean drum, and Himalayan singing bowls for layered harmonics.

Private Session Options

1:1 restorative sessions, couples ceremonies with partner-focused intentions, or corporate immersion for team coherence — all modulated to clients' needs and space acoustics.

VIP Days

Full-day sensory design: space curation, bespoke sound composition, and integrative rituals. Perfect for leadership retreats, artist residencies, or deep personal work with {{FACILITATOR_NAME}}.

Myth vs. Truth

Myth: Sound baths are only about relaxation.
Truth: While deeply relaxing, they are also somatic tools for nervous system regulation, emotional integration, and subtle energetic release.
Myth: You must be spiritual to benefit.
Truth: Our work is secular and sensory-first; benefits are physiological and accessible to anyone open to embodied experience.

Case notes — a short example

A corporate team booked a 90-minute immersion to reduce reactivity before a strategy off-site. We used grounding monochord tones, tuning forks for focus, and guided breath work. Results reported: calmer meetings, clearer listening, and a renewed sense of group cohesion.

FAQ — quick

When is the next public session?

See the Events page for the full calendar. Next event: {{NEXT_EVENT_DATE}}

How long is a typical group session?

Most gatherings run 75–90 minutes, with a long-form sound journey of 40–60 minutes.

Ready to reserve a spot or request a bespoke booking?

We can schedule a quick consultation call to design the exact experience you need.
